records.text: Paper card. Question: How do the electrical and magnetic properties of high-entropy oxides (HEOs) correlate with their composition and configurational entropy?. System: [LaNd](Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Co0.2Ni0.2)O3 perovskites. Processing: solid-state reactions, with initial components mixed in stoichiometric proportions, ground for 3 h, compacted at 3 tons/cm2, and heated at 1300 °C for 10 h. Test conditions: temperatures of 150-450 K, frequencies of 10−1-107 Hz, and magnetic fields of ±3T. Findings: The average particle size of the HEOs critically depends on their chemical composition; The configurational entropy of the HEOs correlates with their magnetic and electrical properties; The HEOs exhibit a semiconducting type of conductivity, with variable range hopping and small polaron hopping conduction mechanisms; The magnetic properties of the HEOs are influenced by the average ionic radius of the A-site cation and the configurational entropy; The HEOs exhibit frustrated magnetic states, with ferromagnetic nanoclusters in a paramagnetic matrix. Mechanism: The correlation between the electrical and magnetic properties of the HEOs is attributed to the configurational entropy and the average ionic radius of the A-site cation, which influence the intensity of the indirect super-exchange interactions and the formation of ferromagnetic nanoclusters. Quote: "Nominal chemical composition of the HEOs correlates well with initial calculated stoichiometry"
